By this award, I shall decide a claim petition under section 166/140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
filed by the petitioners Suman Lata (wife of the deceased) and Jyoti Pal (minor daughter of the deceased) with respect to the death of Manoj Kumar in a motor vehicle accident.
2. The accident in the present case took place on 27.11.2017, at around 09:30 PM.
Manoj Kumar was going to Sector-18 from his office on his motorcycle registration No. UP-16L-7308.

When he reached near GIP Gate No.2, Sector-39, Noida, a tractor registration No.UP-16L- 4527, driven by its driver respondent no. 1 Omesh, in a rash and negligent manner and in high speed, hit his motorcycle.
Due to this Suman Lata versus Omesh Kumar & Others collision, Manoj Kumar died on the spot.

sentences.text: According to the claim petition, Manoj Kumar was working as Senior Electrician (Department Maintenance) with M/s Sagan Hotel Ltd and was earning Rs.14,109/- per month.
The petitioners have claimed Rs.30,00,000/- as compensation for the death of Manoj Kumar in that motor vehicle accident.

3. The respondents no.1 Omesh, the driver of the offending tractor has filed written statement and taken the defence that the accident happened due to the negligence of deceased Manoj Kumar himself because he was driving the motorcycle at a high speed.
He came from the back side and wrong side without blowing any horn and hit the tractor.
He was driving the tractor at a normal speed following all traffic rules.
4. The legal representative of Dropadi who was the owner of the tractor have also filed their written statement in this case.
They have stated that they are not the legal heirs of Dropadi.
She passed away leaving behind her daughter Premwati who also passed away in the year 2014.
Premwati was survived by her husband and two children.

Therefore, the husband of Premwati and her children are Suman Lata vs Omesh Kumar & Others on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116345669/

In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, the Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
12. Now in this case, one of the petitioners, Suman Lata has examined herself as PW-1.
She is the wife of the deceased.

In order to establish their claim, she has proved the documents like copy of PAN card of the deceased as Ex.PW1/1, driving licence of the deceased Ex.PW1/2, her aadhar card Ex.PW1/3, aadhar card of her daughter Ex.PW1/4, certified copy of criminal case Ex.PW1/5, identity card of the deceased Mark X and her PAN card Mark 'Y'.

She has deposed that her husband died in this accident and that the accident was caused due Suman Lata versus Omesh Kumar & Others to rash and negligent act of the respondent no. 1, who was the driver of the tractor.

13. Regarding negligence of the driver of the tractor, PW-3 Anjeet Pal is an important witness.
According to his evidence, on 27.11.2014, at about 09:30 p.m. his brother-in-law Manoj Kumar was going to Sector-18 from his office on his motor cycle No. UP-16L-7308.
He was following Manoj Kumar.

When they reached in-front of GIP Gate No.2, Sector 39, Noida, a tractor registration No.UP-16L-4527, driven by its driver respondent no.1 Omesh, in a very high speed, rash and negligent manner, without blowing any horn and without taking necessary precautions, hit Manoj Kumar with a great force.
Manoj Kumar fell down on the road after the collision and died on the spot.
His postmortem was conducted on the next day.
He also stated that the offending tractor was attached with a trolly.
After the accident even the trolly was overturned.
14. After investigation, the police filed the chargesheet against respondent no. 1 the driver of the tractor.
Filing of chargesheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima faice points to his culpability.

After the death of Dropadi, this tractor was in his exclusive possession and was in his possession on the date of accident and was still in his possession when he deposed in the court.
17. In the backdrop of the testimony of eye witness and the driver of the tractor, it appears that it was the driver of the tractor who was negligent in this accident.
The police investigation has established this fact.
Not only this, he was also negligent and careless in not insuring the vehicle and bringing it on road.
Since it was a tractor, it is not clear that what Omesh Pal was doing with the tractor on road at 9:30 PM in the night, which is a primarily vehicle for agriculture purposes.
The testimony of the eye witness Anjeet Pal inspires confidence that accident occurred due to the negligence of respondent o. 1 driver of the tractor.

18. In view of above, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities of evidence, it is proved that Manoj Kumar died due to rash and Suman Lata versus Omesh Kumar & Others negligent act of respondent no.1 Omesh, the driver of the offending tractor.

It has come in the evidence of respondent no. 1 Omesh Pal that respondent no.2 to 7 are not legal heirs of Dropadi.

In cross examination, he has stated that Dropadi was his grand mother and respondent no. 2 to 5 are the children of brother-in-law (devar of Dropadi) and respondent no. 6 and 7 are the grand sons of Dropadi and are his real brothers.
He denied the suggestions that after the death of Dropadi her properties devolved on respondent no. 2 to 7.

According to section 2(11)
Code of Civil Procedure, a "legal representative" means a person who in law represents the estate of a deceased person, and includes any person who intermeddles with the estate of the deceased and where a party sue or is sued in a representative character the person on whom the estate devolves on the death of the party so suing or sued.
A motorcycle vehicle Act does not define legal representative.
This term has wide meaning and for the purpose of this law will cover all those person who might have inherited from the estate of the deceased.
The petitioner has not Suman Lata versus Omesh Kumar & Others proved anything in this regard.

Since there is no insurance company, all the respondents are liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
